title: Ohio State kicks off 2026 season with full roster and title favorites
seoTitle: Ohio State opens 2026 season as top-ranked title favorite
subtitle: 2024 national champions enter as number one in the rankings and already release the lineup for the first game against Ball State
excerpt: Ohio State starts the 2026 season atop the polls, boasting the nation's best interior offensive line and new faces on defense.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The Buckeyes enter the 2026 season as the No. 1 team in the polls after winning the 2024 national championship. Public interest surged when the program released its full depth chart ahead of the season‑opening game against Ball State, scheduled for Saturday at 12:30 p.m. ET.

Offensive line: interior trio ranked best in the nation

The interior group of Austin Siereveld, Carson Hinzman and Luke Montgomery has been identified as the nation's top interior line. All three were active contributors to the 2024 championship run and started every game last season.

Defense: new faces and rotating safeties

On defense, rookie Jay Timmons appears as the nickel back, while safeties Jaylen McClain and transfer Earl Little are the starters. Terry Moore and Leroy Roker III serve as rotational options, depending on the need to reinforce the secondary.

Line positions: possible debut for John Walker

One of the few remaining questions concerns the nose tackle spot. UCF transfer John Walker could start in place of Will Smith, according to the coaches.

Quarterback: battle between St. Clair and Fahey

Practice has revealed a genuine competition between five‑star veteran St. Clair and three‑star Californian Fahey, who impressed in camp. Both are expected to see action against Ball State, making the second half of the matchup especially intriguing.

Running backs: role for Bey and pass protection

Freshman Bey has drawn optimistic commentary but still lacks a defined role. Coach Carlos Locklyn stresses that he must contribute in blocking as well as running. Veterans Bo Jackson and West, now in their second season, are expected to improve pass protection, while transfer Ja’Kobi Jackson from Florida adds size and experience.

Season outlook

Analysts project Ohio State has the highest chance of winning the national title (14 %) and the second‑highest chance of reaching the College Football Playoff (71 %). Even with what is considered the toughest Big Ten schedule, the team can still secure a playoff berth with a 10‑2 or even a 9‑3 record, thanks to its high talent level.

With information from The New York Times.
